answer: it is NOT concentrated.  Fixing the limiter buys 1.024x, because the next block is 283.5 MHz.  The nine slowest blocks span 276.9 to 409.4 MHz -- 1.48x across EIGHT fixes -- with no single rung worth more than 1.098x.  The design is at a balanced plateau, and further single-block frequency work has almost no leverage.
not_a_claim: a rung's fmax is its best CLOSED record, so a block with no closed record is not on this ladder at all -- 48 of 105 modules are still outside any closed block
the ladder is a bound on the clock, not on token time: a block's cycle count matters as much as its clock, which is exactly what defeats the divider swap
question: the ABI 3.0 clock limiter is ot_a3_hc_sinkhorn20_rne_pipe at 276.9 MHz.  How much clock is actually available above it, and is it concentrated anywhere?

the_one_concentrated_lever.the_replacement_exists: ot_a3_fp32_div_rne_pipe is proven bit-exact on 673 cases and closes at 431.4 MHz against 283.5, which is 1.52x
the_one_concentrated_lever.why: it is the critical path of the limiter itself -- the routed worst path runs entirely inside g_reference_divider.divider, lower_code[0] to result_code[31] -- and it is instantiated by NINE synthesisable modules, so its own frequency bounds all of them
the_one_concentrated_lever.why_it_is_not_simply_swapped: serial use makes it SLOWER.  Inside the Sinkhorn twin it costs 1.55x the reference's cycles over the same 35 matrices, because that FSM issues one division and waits: in_valid is one state and out_ready is the next.  1.55x cycles against a 1.52x clock is a net loss, which is why the parameter defaults off with the number written down.  Hiding the latency needs each consumer to INTERLEAVE independent divisions -- a Sinkhorn group's elements share a denominator and are independent, so it is possible -- and that is a per-site FSM rewrite, not a parameter flip.

what_this_does_not_bound: the iso-area figure.  That comes from ot_compute_unit, which closes ROUTED at 1.290 GHz with zero slew violations; the 276.9 MHz ladder is the ABI 3.0 control and HC blocks.  See results/derived/iso_area_position_against_a100.json.
